ascii/ui, a design system drawn in ASCII

Thirty-six shadcn-style components in an ASCII skin. Frames, fills and shadows are strings of characters. Plain HTML underneath, bad signal on top.

For designers and developers who copy a component and own the code.

0 dependencies. 36 components, 34 in the kit. 2 kit files.

Questions

    

      
Is this accessible?
The characters are paint. Underneath are native controls with labels, focus states and keyboard support, and decorative glyphs are hidden from assistive tech. Reduced motion turns off every animation and every sound.

      
Does it need a framework?
No. The kit is two files, ascii-ui.css and ascii-ui.js. The components are classes and custom properties, so they drop into anything.

      
Why monospace only?
The grid is the design. Every width is a number of characters and every height a number of rows, which is what lets strings work as borders.

      
Can I turn the glitch off?
Yes. The Glitch switch kills it, the slider scales it, and the page respects reduced motion.

      
Who made this?
Fede Kotek designed it. Claude Code built it, in rounds: agents audit, agents fix, and a script decides what ships. The whole story is in How it was made, at the end of this page.

    

  


  

    
How it was made

    
A design system with one material: the character.

    

    
The problem

    
Most component kits look like the same kit. ASCII interfaces look different, and most are screenshots or terminal toys: pure text breaks screen readers and does not reflow on a phone. The brief was a kit made of characters that still works like a kit, with a keyboard, a screen reader, a phone, and copy and paste. The person in charge is a product designer, so every rule had to be one a script can check.


    
By the numbers

    
Counted from the repo and the built site. A script recounts them before every release and fails if this page says otherwise.

The bar is the weight against its cap, 6 kB a #. The seven modes: keyboard, screen reader names, reduced motion, forced colors, more contrast, print, touch.


    
Rules the scripts enforce

    
Each rule has a script, and each script is a step in the release bar. A rule no script checks is a suggestion.

    
Each rule, and the script in the release bar that fails the release when it is broken.
      
RuleScript

      
        
No em dashesfacts.py

        
Cyan is focus onlyfacts.py

        
Columns on the 1ch gridbreakpoints.py

        
Reduced motion means nonereduced.py

        
No setIntervalclock.py

        
Nothing from elsewherebudget.py

        
No tap target under 40pxaudit.py

        
These numbersfacts.py

      
    

    
Em dashes are looked for in the source, the docs, the built site and the commit log. Cyan is read from every CSS rule that paints with it: each one needs a focus state. Taps are drawn at 44px, and the script fails anything under 40.


    
Principles

    
    
      
  • Plain HTML underneath. The characters are paint. A button stays a button, so keyboards and screen readers work.
    • 
      
  • Every frame is a string. A border is one character repeated, so a new character reskins the part.
    • 
      
  • Weight is density. @ is the loudest thing on the page and . is the quietest.
    • 
      
  • One grid, 1ch by 21px. Widths are counts of characters, heights are counts of rows.
    • 
      
  • Glitch is feedback. It fires on touch and on state changes. At rest, the page reads.
    • 
      
  • One file, no dependencies. No framework, no bundler. The site ships as one HTML file and works from file://.
    • 
    


    
Process

    
One HTML file for nine versions. v10 made it a repo, with docs and Playwright scripts for QA.

    
.  v1   HTML on a character grid
:  v2   frames are strings
=  v3   the ring spins
+  v4   glitch, signal palette
   v5   never published
*  v7   18 more parts, Code tabs
#  v8   6 presets, a ramp editor
%  v10  a repo, docs, QA scripts
@  v11  the kit: 2 files, MIT

    
Each row is one step heavier on the ramp. v5 is a space because it never shipped.

    
From v10.8 on, the work ran in rounds. Auditors read the site in parallel, one lens each, and change nothing. Their findings are split by file, so no two builders touch the same one.

    
@ audit   read only, in parallel
:
@ plan    fixes split by file
:
@ build   one worktree each
:
@ review  reviewer and ux-critic
:
@ release every step passes
:
@ ship    main, Vercel, live

    
ROUND   AUDIT       BUILD
v10.8   ########    ##### 8 auditors, 5 builders.
v11.0   ##########  ##### 10 auditors, 5 builders.
v11.1   #######     #### 7 auditors, 4 builders.
v11.2   ##########  ######### 10 auditors, 9 builders.

    
One # is one agent. v11.1 had seven lenses: a UI designer, legibility, copy, a frontend engineer, an interaction bug hunt, the Code tab's truth, and an LLM reading the docs cold. v11.2 went through a UX checklist: print, high contrast, touch, security, share cards, and four new overlays.

    
The release bar is one command. It runs 22 steps and stops at the first failure.

    
[@] clean at 2 sizes, 2 themes
[@] the shipped file loads clean
[@] the Code tab prints the kit
[@] 11 widths, 360 to 1920
[@] one animation clock
[@] no tiny taps, no tiny text
[@] no surprise phone keyboard
[@] every kit part, pasted twice
[@] every Usage tab holds true
[@] reduced motion, both builds
[@] every address lands
[@] the docs match the code
[@] what ships is what builds
[@] every number on this page
[@] under the size budget

release: ok


    
What did not work

    
    
      
  • A masonry gallery. It packed the cards tight and broke the alphabetical order the index promised. It lasted 29 minutes.
    • 
      
  • The phone menu. The second patch made it worse, so it was rebuilt instead.
    • 
      
  • Three views: Play, Apps and One pager. They read as a portfolio, and this is a kit.
    • 
      
  • Thirty bitmap titles in a row. A wall of shouting. Now there is one per page.
    • 
      
  • A Try it strip on Home. It lasted nine hours.
    • 
      
  • A Code tab that printed the site's own engine. Now it prints the kit, and a script pastes every component twice into a blank page to prove it works.
    • 
      
  • Still not done: the WebGL CRT pass, Safari and Firefox on real devices, and an audit by someone who uses a screen reader.
    •

Rules

    

    
@@ %% ## ** ++ == :: ..

    
    
      
  • Weight is character density. @ is the loudest thing on the page and . is the quietest.
    • 
      
  • Frames, rules, fills and shadows are strings of characters. Hierarchy comes from which character.
    • 
      
  • Big type is a bitmap: every pixel of a headline is a block of characters.
    • 
      
  • Color is signal: magenta acts and marks the worst state, cyan focuses, lime confirms, yellow warns.
    • 
      
  • Glitch is feedback. It fires when you touch something or when a state changes, and the slider turns it down to zero.
    • 
      
  • Everything arrives broken and fixes itself: elements glitch in as they enter the screen, text decodes left to right.
    • 
      
  • Sound is feedback too. Square-wave blips and crushed noise, never music.
    • 
      
  • Nothing jumps. State changes travel through the ramp, one character at a time, at a low frame rate.
    • 
      
  • Underneath it is plain HTML: buttons, inputs, a dialog.
    • 
    

  


  

    
Foundations

    

    
What every component is made of: 14 color tokens, one grid, a ramp of nine steps (space to @), eight tones and six states. Presets in Themes swap the colors. The rest stays put.

Grid

      
One cell is 1ch wide and one row tall. Every width is a number of cells and every height a number of rows.

      

        
Cell
1ch by 21px, the row. CSS reads it as var(--r), JS as A.ROW.

        
Type
Geist Mono, 14px on 21px, at every width. Charts are 12px on 14px.

        
Weights
300 body text. 400 gray text, the bar, the sidebar. 700 frames, slabs, titles.

        
Targets
44px to tap: one row plus 12px above and below.

      


      
Ramp

      
Weight is density. The ramp is nine steps, space to @, and the index is how loud a character is. The ramp editor in Themes swaps the characters, not the order.

      
The ramp, space to at sign, index 0 to 8, with what each step is for.
        
CharacterIndexFor

        
          
 0 spaceNothing. Air.

          
.1 dotThe quietest mark. Tracks, dots, empty cells.

          
:2 colonShadows, wires, the sides of a light rim.

          
=3 equalsThe light rim. Buttons and fields at rest.

          
+4 plusFills on the way up.

          
*5 starFills, chart marks.

          
#6 hashWalls. Cards.

          
%7 percentDense. A primary button under the pointer.

          
@8 atThe loudest. Primary, focus, nodes.

        


      
Tones

      
A frame is one character repeated. The tone class names which one. Five tones use ramp characters. Faint, danger and error use -, / and !, which are not on the ramp.

      
Frame tones: class name, character, what it is for.
        
tone-CharacterFor

        
          
heavy@@@@@@@@at. Primary buttons, focus.

          
dense%%%%%%%%percent. A primary button under the pointer.

          
mid########hash. Cards, and any button under the pointer.

          
light========equals. Buttons and fields at rest.

          
shade::::::::colon. Shadows under cards.

          
faint- - - - -. Empty states, disabled.

          
danger/////////. Destructive actions.

          
error!!!!!!!!!. A field that is wrong.

        


      
States

      
What each form component draws in each state. A dash means it has no such state. Blue is only ever focus.

      
States per form component: default, hover, focus, active, disabled, error.

Recipe

    

    
Sunday asado. Change the servings and the quantities follow, in metric.

    
Asado de domingo

      
6 people

      
    
      
    1. Light the fire 90 minutes before anyone is hungry.
    2. Embers, not flames. Hand test at grill height: 6 seconds.
    3. Bone side down first. Salt, patience, no flipping for sport.
    4. Provoleta goes last. Chorizos go to whoever is complaining.

    Six presets, six color roles, four support shades and one ramp. Change any of them and the whole site follows. Copy the tokens when you like what you see.
    

  
    
    
    Presets
    
    
    
    
    Pick a signal. The page is the preview.
    
    
    
  
    


  
    
    
    Colors
    
    
    
    
    Every color has a job: surface, text, action, focus, success, warning. The four support shades follow the preset.
    
    
    
    
    
  
    


  
    
    
    Ramp
    
    
    
    
    Nine steps, space to @, lightest to heaviest. Every frame, fill, chart and explosion is an index into them. Swap the characters and you have a different kit.
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    Classic ramp.
    
  
    


  
    
    
    Tokens
    
    
    
    
    The theme you are looking at, as CSS. Paste it after ascii-ui.css, or download tokens.css for a page. For Figma or Tokens Studio, download tokens.json: both modes, the grid, the ramp and the motion.
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
  
    


  
    
    
    Signal
    
    
    
    
    The bad signal, for your own pages: four effects an element asks for with data-aui-signal, then two kinds of scanlines for the whole page. Nothing runs until asked. Reduced motion, high contrast and print keep all of it still.
    
    
    
      
    
      
    
        
        
    A state change breaks up for two frames, then sits still. Press the button.
    
        
    
      
    
      
    
        
        
    Words decode into place once, when they come on screen. A screen reader gets the words, never the noise.
    
        
    Twelve probes, three regions, one pager. Nothing is down.
    
        
      
    
      
    
        
        
    A tracking band rolls through now and then. It is see-through and takes no clicks.
    
        
    Channel 3. The picture holds, mostly.
    The band passes. The words stay.
    
        
      
    
      
    
        
        
    Leave the page alone for four seconds and the frame decays. Touch anything and it is back.
    
        
    Nobody has touched this in a while.
    
      
    
      
    
        
        
        
    The crt class on the root, over the whole page. Subtle by design: on a dark theme they sit mostly in the text. Interlace draws every other line, fainter. Neither moves.
    
      
    
    
    
    
    
  
    

  
    
    
    Labs
    
    
    
    
    Five small labs. Each one is a piece of the system you can poke.
    

    
    The ramp
    
    
    Brightness picks the character. Drag across the patch to move the light, and use the slider to change the exposure.
    
    
    
    
    
      
      
      60
    
    

    
    Frames are strings
    
    
    A border is one long string clipped by overflow. Type any character and the frame rebuilds itself out of it.
    
    
    
      
      
    >
    
    
    
    
    Made of #
    

    
    Type is a bitmap
    
    
    Headlines are a 5 by 7 pixel face where every pixel is four characters. Type up to eight and watch it develop.
    
    
    
      
      
    >
    
    
    
    
    

    
    The glitch engine
    
    
    Four effects, fired one at a time. On the rest of the page they fire on their own when state changes.
    
    
    
      
      
      
      
    
    

    
    Sound is oscillators
    
    
    No audio files. Square waves for blips, a sawtooth for errors and filtered noise for the glitches.
